# iatrome

> iatrome (pronounced EYE-uh-trohm, /ˈaɪ.ə.troʊm/) is a free multiplayer party game about bodies, doctors, hospitals and the long, strange history of medicine. Everyone plays on a phone or laptop in a browser. A shared screen (a TV, a laptop, a video call) makes it better, but it's optional. No app, no account, no download. It makes fun of medicine, never of patients.

The name comes from the Greek *iatros*, physician. The humor is dry: questionable historical cures, bureaucracy, bodily betrayals, and the gap between what doctors say and what they mean.

## How it works

- A host opens [iatrome.com/host](https://iatrome.com/host), picks a game, and chooses where everyone is looking: a big screen, or just phones.
- The room gets a 6-letter code, a QR code and a share link. Players join at [iatrome.com](https://iatrome.com) or go straight to `iatrome.com/CODE`.
- Everyone answers, draws and votes on their phone. The show is hosted by Beep, a deadpan pager with a face.
- With a big screen, it carries the prompts, reveals and scoreboard. Without one, every phone shows them instead, and the host's phone gets the host controls. If a laptop joins or drops out mid-game, the phones adjust on their own.
- Rooms can have an optional password. Hosts can lock the room, kick or ban players, and hide any answer from the screen.
- Free to play. No sign-up. Rooms disappear on their own after 30 minutes of nobody being in them.

## Games

- **Grand Rounds** (3–8 players): anonymous head-to-head comedy. Two players answer the same prompt, everyone else votes, authors are revealed after. Round two is more head-to-head quips at double points; the finale is one prompt that everyone answers, with the whole room voting.
- **Didactics Mode** (2–40 players): trivia for big groups and family gatherings, in random teams or everyone for themselves. Everyone answers on their phone or laptop; streaks and the fastest right answer earn bonus points. Late arrivals join the smallest team.
- **Sketch** (3–10 players): one person draws a word live on their phone, everyone else races to guess it.
- **Pick Your Poison** (3–20 players): would you rather, plus guessing what the room picked. Whoever ends up in the minority has to defend themselves to the room.

## Modes

- **Normal**: for anyone. No medical knowledge required; grandparents welcome.
- **Pro**: for people who work or train in healthcare. More jargon, more in-jokes, fewer explanations.

## Pages

- [Home](https://iatrome.com): enter a room code to join.
- [Host a game](https://iatrome.com/host): pick a game and open a room, with or without a big screen.
- `https://iatrome.com/CODE`: short link that drops a player straight into room CODE.

## Good to know

- Works in modern mobile browsers (iOS Safari, Android Chrome) and on desktop. For remote play, share the big screen on any video call.
- All prompts, trivia and drawing words are original. Trivia answers are fact-checked against published sources. It is a game, not medical advice. If something hurts, see an actual clinician, not a pager with opinions.
